transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-11-16
- Time: 11:00 AM UTC
- Duration: ~45m
- Attendees: Carlos (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jared, Mei, Anita (Thermionix)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Weekly POC snapshot focusing on latency/throughput vs incumbent provider.
- Discussed p95/p99 traces, routing/fallback playbook, quantization trade-offs and dedicated slot options.
- Agreed next steps: share traces, run high-concurrency synthetic, pricing addendum.

Topics: benchmarking, latency p95/p99, throughput scaling, KV cache/ prefix caching, routing/fallback, dedicated vs hosted, SOC2/KMS note.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Carlos Mendez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on for about 45 minutes, agenda is quick — recap last week's lab, share the bench snapshot, then tuning items and next steps.
[00:12] Anita Rao: yep, thanks carlos. we had the infrastack change yesterday, so Jared's going to summarize the baseline run differences.
[00:18] Jared Lin: cool, yeah so quick note, incumbent run used their managed endpoint with autoscale, we re-ran the same traffic pattern — 40ms nominal tail on their p50 but p95 ballooned in bursts up to 480. our Redwood runs are averaging lower p95 but there are a couple of tails we need to explain.
[00:40] Priya Nair: to add, we saw consistent throughput improvements when we enabled prefix caching and turned on the lighter quantization profile; cpu offload helped a bit too. note: our 'prefix cache' logs show KV cash hits were about 34% which reduces per-token work.
[01:05] Mei Huang: when you say 'lighter quant', you mean 8-bit dynamic? any impact on output quality we've seen?
[01:12] Priya Nair: yes 8-bit dynamic/awq style profile — we ran evals on the prompt set, small deg of paraphrase variance but within your QA thresholds; we'll share the eval spreadsheet.
[01:30] Jared Lin: the main question for us is consistent p99 under sustained load. IncumbentCloud had built-in regional failover, that masked spikes. how does Redwood's routing and fallback behave under the same pattern?
[01:45] Carlos Mendez: good question. routing's policy based: we can route by latency SLO or cost. in the POC we've been using latency-first route with a cost-fallback to a slightly quantized variant. if regional saturations occur we can fallback to lower-cost model or a replica in another region — there's an automated fallback chain.
[02:05] Anita Rao: is cross-region failover feasible inside your private deployment? networking constraints might make that difficult.
[02:12] Priya Nair: for Private (VPC) deployments cross-region is possible but needs networking peering and IP allowlists; for the hosted POC we simulated failover by spinning a replica in eu-west and triggering a traffic shift. it does add a few ms of RTT which explains some p95 delta.
[02:35] Mei Huang: any specifics on mem/cpu utilization per slot during the 300rps sustained window? Jared, you had numbers?
[02:42] Jared Lin: yeah on the Redwood instance mem peaked at 78% and GPU util stayed near 63% average with bursts to 85% during KV cache misses. Incumbent runs showed higher baseline CPU but lower GPU utilization which implies different batching.
[03:05] Priya Nair: exactly — incumbent uses small fixed batches which decreases variance at the cost of throughput. Redwood's cont-batching is workload-aware so for long sequences you get better throughput but occasionally more p95 variance if the batch assembly waits.
[03:30] Carlos Mendez: and that's where the autoscaling and burst slots come in — we can pre-provision dedicated slots for steady traffic and allow burst capacity to absorb spikes. pricing note will cover that.
[03:45] Jared Lin: about KV cash again — there were a few misses in the middle of the run, what pattern caused that? was it eviction due to different prompt prefixes?
[03:55] Priya Nair: yes some eviction due to variable prefixes; suggestion: canonicalize prefixes on the client side and we can increase cache TTL or pin frequently used keys. also we observed a small issue where prompts with dynamic session ids bypassed cache.
[04:12] Mei Huang: that'll be our fault, we have session ids in the front of the prompt — we can refactor to move them to metadata.
[04:18] Priya Nair: that will immediately increase hit rate. we'll attach a quick snippet to do that.
[04:30] Anita Rao: security question — we need KMS integration and audit logs retained 90 days; are those in the current private build?
[04:38] Carlos Mendez: yes KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Private; audit logs streaming to your SIEM is supported. for the hosted POC we provided masked logs with redaction. we'll include SOC 2 evidence and the audit retention options in the package.
[04:58] Jared Lin: thanks. next: p95/p99 traces — can you walk through the specific anomaly at 19:42 in the run?
[05:05] Priya Nair: looking at the trace, there's an extended KV miss followed by a recompile cycle due to a fallback to a different kernel path for long sequences; that added ~210ms. it's rare but reproducible. our mitigation is to pin kernel selection and pre-warm the KV for those prompts.
[05:30] Mei Huang: recompile? is that runtime JITing?
[05:33] Priya Nair: it's kernel selection + small reprofiling, not heavy JIT, but still adds overhead. we can avoid it by aligning batch shape distributions.
[05:50] Carlos Mendez: operationally, two options: 1) pre-warm and pin kernels (slight memory cost), 2) use dedicated slot to guarantee kernel availability. both are supported.
[06:05] Anita Rao: what about the output quality delta when you push heavier quant — we can't accept regressions above 2% on our eval metric.
[06:12] Priya Nair: under the AWQ/8-bit profile we measured 0.8% drop on your eval while reducing per-token latency by ~15% and cost by ~22%. full details in the eval spreadsheet.
[06:30] Jared Lin: ok good. for throughput: at 10k concurrent synthetic what did Redwood hit vs incumbent? numbers?
[06:38] Priya Nair: in the synthetic we configured 10k concurrency but spread across 10 app instances. Redwood sustained 9,200 rps steady with p95 around 240ms; the incumbent sustained 7,400 rps with p95 near 310ms under same load pattern. note these are lab numbers, network/RTT differences may change production margins.
[07:05] Mei Huang: interesting. did you control for batching window/timeouts?
[07:08] Priya Nair: yes we matched batch timeouts and max batch sizes to mimic incumbent settings. Redwood's dynamic batching leaned into larger batches for short sequences which improved throughput.
[07:25] Carlos Mendez: we should surface the exact bench config in the shared folder — Priya will drop the config.
[07:30] Anita Rao: can Redwood match the incumbent's regional failover? if not, that's a blocker for us.
[07:36] Carlos Mendez: we can match it, but with caveats: private network constraints may increase failover latency. in hosted/demo we used a cross-region replica and an active-passive routing with health probes; that model can be implemented for Private with your networking team.
[07:55] Jared Lin: on monitoring, how do you surface token-level cost? Anita wants clarity on unit economics.
[08:02] Priya Nair: Console exposes per-route and per-model token cost, including rollup to application keys. you can drill to p50/p95 latency vs token consumption and dedupe cold-starts. we'll share a short demo clip.
[08:20] Mei Huang: one more perf question: did you test with long-context (4k) vs short (1k)? how does p95 change?
[08:27] Priya Nair: yes long-context increases KV pressure and increases p95 by ~30-40% in our runs if caching isn't tuned. with caching and pinned kernels, we get within 10-12% of short-context p95.
[08:45] Carlos Mendez: quick pause for clarifying next steps and priorities — Anita what's your main gating criterion this week?
[08:52] Anita Rao: consistent p99 under sustained load and documentation of security posture. if both look good we can move to decision to trial a dedicated slot.
[09:02] Carlos Mendez: perfect. so action items above reflect that.
[09:10] Jared Lin: can you also provide a planned canary rollback playbook? incumber — sorry incumbent— has an easy rollback that ops likes.
[09:18] Priya Nair: yes we have a canary + automatic fallback policy; we will share a one-page runbook with health checks, thresholds, and sample curl checks.
[09:30] Mei Huang: good, that helps.
[09:35] Anita Rao: any unexpected findings from the lab that we should be aware of?
[09:39] Priya Nair: aside from the kernel-selection tail and the prefix caching misses, two minor items: 1) one micro-benchmark showed slightly higher latency for very short sequences due to our assembly time — fixable with a micro-config tweak; 2) some of your prompts contain dynamic IDs which reduced cache hit rate.
[10:00] Carlos Mendez: ok let's log those as short-term fixes.
[10:05] --- mid-call deep-dive (15–30m): Priya shows a live trace and Jared asks specific timestamped questions; some transcribed lines below are paraphrased or imperfect.
[15:12] Priya Nair: (screen) here's the p95 trace; you can see the spike at 19:42 — that's KV miss + small kernel switch. we've flagged it in the runbook with mitigation steps.
[18:30] Jared Lin: we've got a follow-up — can you export raw traces in zip and include flamegraphs?
[18:36] Priya Nair: yes we'll export flamegraphs and the raw traces.
[22:05] Mei Huang: does Redwood support SSO/SAML for console access? some of our testers need SSO.
[22:12] Carlos Mendez: yes SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning are supported. for Private installs we can integrate with your IDP.
[22:30] Anita Rao: retention and legal — what's your default PII redaction for hosted logs?
[22:36] Carlos Mendez: hosted POC will redact PII by default; for Private we can do no-redaction if you request and have the necessary controls. we'll add the exact retention policy to the doc.
[23:00] Jared Lin: ok, regarding the high-concurrency run next week, we'd like Redwood to run a mirrored config from the incumbent including same request distribution so we can compare apples-to-apples.
[23:08] Priya Nair: understood — please share the incumbent request distribution and we'll mirror it.
[23:15] Anita Rao: can you scope the dedicated slot cost for our expected sustained baseline of 6k rps?
[23:22] Carlos Mendez: yes — Carlos will share pricing addendum; short answer: dedicated slot + burst pool matches your 6k steady with buffer for spikes, exact numbers in the doc.
[24:05] Mei Huang: on a smaller note — some words in the earlier generated summaries spelled Redwood product names wrong, can that be corrected? we saw 'Redwoodify' in a note.
[24:12] Priya Nair: ha, those are auto-typo artifacts; we'll correct them before sharing.
[24:30] --- final 10 minutes: recap and explicit next steps.
[34:00] Carlos Mendez: recap — Priya will upload traces, configs, flamegraphs and bench scripts by 2027-11-18. Jared will run the 10k concurrency test and push logs by 2027-11-20. Carlos will send pricing and SLA addendum by 2027-11-17.
[34:20] Anita Rao: once we review those, we'll decide on a short dedicated-slot pilot.
[34:28] Mei Huang: can we schedule a 30-minute check-in after the synthetic run?
[34:33] Carlos Mendez: yes propose 2027-11-22 1500 UTC?
[34:37] Anita Rao: works for us.
[34:40] Jared Lin: one more thing — will you include a short comparison table vs IncumbentCloud showing p95/p99 and unit cost?
[34:48] Priya Nair: yes we'll include a head-to-head table in the shared doc.
[34:55] Carlos Mendez: great. thanks everyone. we'll share artifacts and next steps.
[35:02] Anita Rao: thanks all, bye.

Meeting end.
